stories.headline: Russia hits Kyiv with ballistic missiles for second time in a week, killing at least 11

key_facts.fact: Russia launched 419 air-attack weapons at Ukraine overnight July 5-6 — 68 missiles and 351 drones — with Kyiv the main target.
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 419 air attack weapons were recorded—68 missiles and 351 UAVs of various types. The main target of the attack was Kyiv.

key_facts.fact: 29 ballistic missiles (including anti-ship missiles) struck 34 locations; none of the ballistic missiles were shot down.
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 29 ballistic missiles (including anti-ship missiles) and 18 attack UAVs were recorded striking 34 locations... none of the ballistic missiles were shot down.

key_facts.fact: As of 8:30 a.m., Ukrainian air defenses had shot down or neutralized 363 targets — 37 missiles and 326 drones.
key_facts.excerpt: As of 8:30 a.m., air defense forces have shot down or neutralized 363 targets—37 missiles and 326 drones of various types.

key_facts.fact: ABC News reported at least 14 killed across Kyiv and the surrounding region with around 60 wounded; LIGA reported 11 killed in Kyiv alone.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 14 people were killed in Kyiv and the surrounding region, with around 60 more wounded, he said. Russia fired 68 missiles and 351 attack drones.

key_facts.fact: It was the second Russian strike on Kyiv in under a week, following an attack last week that killed more than 30 people; the assault came on the eve of a NATO summit in Ankara.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia has fired missiles and drones into apartment buildings in Kyiv for the second time in a week... just days after another Russian attack killed more than 30 people in Kyiv.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky urged NATO to take 'strong decisions' on air defenses; officials said Ukraine has insufficient interceptors to stop ballistic missiles, which Russia is increasingly exploiting.
key_facts.excerpt: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged the alliance to take 'strong decisions' on boosting Ukraine's air defences... Ukraine's army had shot down the Russian drones and cruise missiles, but had 'insufficient supply of interceptor missiles' to stop the ballistic missiles.

stories.headline: Trump to meet Zelensky at NATO summit in Ankara as US presses allies on 5% defense spending

key_facts.fact: The White House said on July 5 that Trump will hold bilateral meetings with Ukraine's Zelensky and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa on the sidelines of the NATO summit in Ankara on Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: 'On Wednesday afternoon, President Trump will participate in bilateral meetings with President Zelensky of Ukraine and President al-Sharaa of the Syrian Arab Republic,' Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly said.

key_facts.fact: Trump departs Washington Monday evening, arrives in Ankara Tuesday to meet Erdogan, then joins the NATO leaders' working session Wednesday before the bilaterals.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump will depart the White House on Monday evening and arrive in the Turkish capital Ankara on Tuesday afternoon... On Wednesday, Trump will join an official welcome, family photo and NATO leaders' working session, before holding separate bilateral meetings with Zelenskyy and Sharaa.

key_facts.fact: US Ambassador to NATO Matt Whitaker said Trump 'fully expects that all allies will step up immediately and get on the path to 5%' defense spending, seeking to enforce last year's pledge.
key_facts.excerpt: 'President Trump fully expects that all allies will step up immediately and get on the path to 5% and do it with urgency,' Matt Whitaker, the U.S. ambassador to NATO, told reporters.

key_facts.fact: Trump spoke by phone with both Zelensky and Putin on July 4; a US official said Trump would 'follow up' with Putin after meeting Zelensky about ending the war.
key_facts.excerpt: Both Putin and Zelensky spoke by phone with Trump on July 4... Trump would 'follow up' with Russian President Vladimir Putin afterwards, the official said.

key_facts.fact: The summit comes as Trump seeks to end the nearly four-and-a-half-year war, with the war in its fifth year expected to be a key focus in Ankara.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump will meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at a NATO summit in Turkey on Wednesday that will be charged with tension over the U.S. leader's views on Greenland, European defense spending and the Iran war.

stories.headline: OPEC+ raises August output by 188,000 bpd as oil slides back to pre-war levels

key_facts.fact: Seven OPEC+ producers — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman — agreed at a July 5 virtual meeting to raise output by a combined 188,000 barrels per day in August.
key_facts.excerpt: OPEC+ said on Sunday that seven member countries – Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman – would raise output by 188,000 barrels per day from August.

key_facts.fact: It is the fifth consecutive monthly increase, continuing the gradual unwinding of voluntary cuts the group first announced in 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: It is the fifth consecutive month that members of the alliance have agreed to open the oil taps a little wider... continues the gradual unwinding of voluntary cuts the same countries announced back in 2023.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude was trading below $72 a barrel as markets opened Sunday night — roughly its pre-war level — with WTI near $68, far below March peaks near $120.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude, the international benchmark, was trading below $72 a barrel... The US benchmark, WTI, was trading even lower at around $68 a barrel.

key_facts.fact: Total OPEC+ production had dropped to 33.13 million bpd in May from 42.77 million in February after the Strait of Hormuz closure; supply is now recovering following the US-Iran ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: Total OPEC+ production dropped to 33.13 million bpd in May, down from 42.77 million bpd in February, according to OPEC figures.

key_facts.fact: The producers said they retain flexibility to pause or reverse the increases and are scheduled to meet again on August 2.
key_facts.excerpt: The seven countries reaffirmed... they retain full flexibility to increase, pause, or reverse the phase-out of the voluntary cuts... The seven countries are scheduled to meet next on August 2, 2026.

stories.headline: Wildfires scorch 17,000 hectares across France, Spain and Portugal as heatwave returns

key_facts.fact: Wildfires devastated more than 17,000 hectares across France, Spain and Portugal, with temperatures forecast to reach 40C on July 5 and the heatwave set to push north on Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: The latest wildfires have already devastated more than 17,000 hectares of land across France, Spain and Portugal where temperatures in some places are forecast to reach 40C.

key_facts.fact: In central Portugal's Vouzela area, more than 1,200 firefighters battled a blaze that had burned 12,000 hectares since Thursday; Spain sent 120 firefighters and Italy and Spain dispatched water-bombing aircraft.
key_facts.excerpt: In central Portugal's Vouzela area, more than 1,200 firefighters backed up by nearly 400 vehicles and 15 aircraft tried to put out a blaze... had burned across an area of 12,000 hectares by Sunday.

key_facts.fact: Greek fire services responded to 60 wildfires in a 24-hour period, with a fast-moving blaze near Thessaloniki triggering evacuation alerts for three suburbs.
key_facts.excerpt: Greek fire services responded to 60 separate wildfires across the country over a single 24-hour period on Saturday, testing the limits of emergency resources.

key_facts.fact: In the US, at least 19 deaths in New Jersey were suspected to be heat-related, and about 900,000 utility customers lost power as severe storms followed the heat dome.
key_facts.excerpt: Several days of scorching temperatures are suspected to have caused at least 19 deaths in New Jersey... About 900,000 utility customers... were without electricity early Sunday afternoon.

key_facts.fact: France recorded more than 2,000 excess deaths in one week during June's heatwave, while Spain and Belgium each reported more than 1,000.
key_facts.excerpt: France said there had been more than 2,000 extra deaths than usual in just one week, while Spain and Belgium each reported more than 1,000.

stories.headline: Netanyahu: no Gaza reconstruction until Hamas disarms, as US reportedly drops precondition

key_facts.fact: At the July 5 weekly cabinet meeting, Netanyahu said 'there will be no reconstruction in Gaza without dismantling and demilitarizing the Strip.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'There will be no reconstruction in Gaza without dismantling and demilitarizing the Strip,' Netanyahu said.

key_facts.fact: His remarks responded to a report that the US administration had decided to drop Hamas' disarmament as a formal precondition for reconstruction; Netanyahu did not deny the report.
key_facts.excerpt: Netanyahu responded to a ynet report that the U.S. administration had decided to drop Hamas' disarmament as a formal precondition for Gaza's reconstruction. Netanyahu did not deny the report.

key_facts.fact: The US plan, announced earlier this year, includes a Palestinian technocratic governing mechanism and an international framework to oversee reconstruction.
key_facts.excerpt: The plan, announced by the Trump administration earlier this year, includes the creation of a Palestinian technocratic governing mechanism for the Strip and an international framework to oversee reconstruction.

key_facts.fact: The IDF confirmed it now controls about 60% of the Gaza Strip, up from the 53% agreed in last year's ceasefire, as the 'Yellow Line' has been moved deeper into the enclave.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel now controls 60 per cent of Gaza, its military has confirmed, up from the 53 per cent agreed to in last year's ceasefire negotiations.

stories.headline: Ripple wins full MiCA license in Luxembourg, unlocking crypto services across 30 EEA countries

key_facts.fact: Ripple announced on July 6 it received full Crypto-Asset Service Provider (CASP) authorization under the EU's MiCA regulation from Luxembourg's financial regulator, the CSSF.
key_facts.excerpt: Ripple announced that it has received full Crypto Asset Service Provider (CASP) authorization under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation from Luxembourg's financial authority.

key_facts.fact: The license lets Ripple passport custody, transfer and exchange services from Luxembourg into all 30 EEA countries without approval from each national regulator.
key_facts.excerpt: Now with full CASP status, Ripple can passport its services from Luxembourg into all 30 countries in the European Economic Area, which includes the 27 EU member states plus Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein.

key_facts.fact: The authorization follows a preliminary 'Green Light Letter' from the CSSF on June 23; the MiCA transition period expired July 1, barring unlicensed firms from most regulated crypto services in the EU.
key_facts.excerpt: On June 23, Ripple announced preliminary CASP approval from Luxembourg's Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)... As of July 1, the MiCA transition period expired, so companies without approval can no longer lawfully offer most regulated crypto services in the EU.

key_facts.fact: Combined with its EU Electronic Money Institution license, Ripple can now offer end-to-end crypto payments to European institutions; it says it holds more than 75 regulatory licenses globally.
key_facts.excerpt: Combined with the EU Electronic Money Institution licence the company obtained from the same regulator earlier this year, the approval means Ripple can now offer its complete end-to-end crypto payments infrastructure... The approval adds to a global portfolio of more than 75 regulatory licences.

stories.headline: UK's MHRA approves Retifanlimab, first treatment for advanced Merkel cell skin cancer

key_facts.fact: On July 6 the MHRA approved Retifanlimab (ZYNYZ) as the first treatment for adults with advanced Merkel cell carcinoma that has spread or returned and cannot be cured by surgery or radiotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: The MHRA has today (6 July 2026) approved Retifanlimab (ZYNYZ) as the first treatment given to adults with advanced Merkel cell skin cancer that has spread or returned and cannot be cured with an operation or radiotherapy.

key_facts.fact: Retifanlimab is an immunotherapy that blocks a pathway cancer cells use to evade the immune system; it is given as a 30-minute intravenous infusion.
key_facts.excerpt: Retifanlimab works by helping the body's immune system recognise and attack cancer cells. It blocks a pathway that cancer cells can use to avoid being detected... administered via diluted intravenous infusion over 30 minutes.

key_facts.fact: In a study of 101 previously untreated adults, 53.5% responded to Retifanlimab — 16.8% with no detectable cancer and 36.6% with tumour shrinkage — with responses typically lasting just over two years.
key_facts.excerpt: In a study of 101 adults... 53.5% of patients responded to treatment with Retifanlimab. Of these, 16.8% had no detectable signs of cancer... while 36.6% experienced tumour shrinkage... the response typically lasted just over two years.

key_facts.fact: The approval was granted to Incyte Biosciences UK Ltd via the International Recognition Procedure.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval was granted on 6 July 2026 to Incyte Biosciences UK Ltd. This product was submitted and approved via International Recognition Procedure (IRP).

sources.title: MHRA approves Retifanlimab (ZYNYZ) for the treatment of advanced Merkel cell skin cancer
